utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: May I ask the registrar to call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is case number IT-06-90-PT, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, Ivan Cermak and Mladen Markac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. And I welcome --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. Welcome all to this Status Conference. The accused, the correct name for the accused would be Gotovina?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. And I also would like to have General Gotovina to confirm that he can follow the proceedings in a language that he understands? THE ACCUSED GOTOVINA: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Indeed I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then for appearances. For the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Alan Tieger and Laurie Sartorio, with our case manager, Donnica Henry-Frijlink for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence, Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. Good afternoon, Your Honour, Gregory Kehoe. And to my immediate right Luka Misetic, and my far right Payam Akhavn for General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: For Ivan Cermak. And again do I pronounce his name correctly, Cermak?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, Your Honour. Good afternoon. I am attorney-at-law Cedo Prodanovic, joined here today by attorney-at-law by Jadranka Slokovic representing Mr. Cermak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. Welcome. And then for Mladen Markac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. I'm attorney-at-law Miroslav Separovic. I have with me today Mr. Goran Mikulicic and our case manager Vladimir Radonic on behalf of General Markac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. Welcome. Well, as you know, there has been -- this case has now been assigned to a new pre-trial Chamber, a new Chamber, and you are well aware of the composition of that Chamber. And I have been then assigned as Pre-trial Judge in this case. The accused Cermak and Markac are on provisional release and therefore are not present here today. As for the reasons for Status Conference, first that all parties here are well aware of that, to organise exchanges between the parties, to ensure an expeditious preparation for trial, and to allow the accused to raise issues in relation to his or her mental and physical condition. In preparation of this Status Conference, a Rule 65 ter conference took place yesterday, and I have been briefed about the discussions held during that conference. At the latest Status Conference, many of the issues raised were waiting for a decision on joinder to be issued. And now, since 14 July 2006, the issue on joinder has been decided on by the Trial Chamber and the cases were joined. This decision is now under appeal. What I propose is that we go through some items that we have identified, together with the assistance of counsel. And of course the parties will then have the opportunity to raise any additional issues that may be relevant for discussion. As for outstanding motions, we have first Gotovina preliminary motion to dismiss the proposed joinder indictment, pursuant to Rule 72, filed on 28 April 2006. I just want to make a statement that the Trial Chamber has received all consequent -- all subsequent filings of the parties, and that a decision by the Trial Chamber will be taken once the appeals Chamber has decided on the interlocutory appeal from the decision of 14 July 2006. Secondly, a motion for extension of time and for clarification of order and decision on non-disclosure of the supporting material, dated 14 July 2006, filed on 31 August 2006. As I understand it, counsel for Gotovina indicated to the Prosecution and confirmed yesterday at the 65 ter meeting or conference that he does not object to the Prosecution's motion. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: And the decision will be issued shortly. This is of course before -- a motion before the Chamber as such and not for me to decide as the Pre-trial Judge. Judge Kwon is abroad this week, and he will be back in The Hague Monday, and we will deal with this as soon as the Chamber is -- the full Chamber. I also noted that from the motion by the Prosecution that the need for time, the extent of time required, occurred defer, would defer, dependent on what result this clarification will give, but I think we can leave that safely with the Chamber and by -- the discretion of the Chamber, once the results of this clarification is clear, to evaluate whether this extension 18 September would be sufficient or not. I don't know if you have any comments on that, on the Prosecution side?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I agree with the Court. It's probably not necessary to supplement the motion orally at this time. If the need for clarification arises, we're always prepared to do so, but I share the Court's view, that at this point we can move forward as it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: And Defence teams?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: On behalf of General Gotovina, we agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Defence team for -- sorry, Defence team for Cermak.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we agree, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: And Markac?

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Likewise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. The next thing on my agenda here is disclosure. I understand from the briefing I got from the 65 ter conference, generally speaking, that the disclosure has reached the same stage practically in relation to the three accused, but we will go through these different disclosures together now. And Rule 66(A)(i) is complete, but subject to the action to be taken by the Prosecution under this, the decision of non-disclosure of 14 July 2006 in relation to the accused Gotovina. The Chamber understands that the supporting materials have been disclosed to all accused, and Rule 66(A)(i) or, when, is therefore complete, subject to the thing I mentioned, and a decision will, as I said, be issued shortly on the motion of 31 August. Do the parties have anything more to add on this item. Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Nothing to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Defence teams?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Nothing on behalf of General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing on behalf of General Cermak either, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same applies to General Markac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Then it is Rule 62(A)(ii). And I have been informed that most of the disclosure under this Rule has been made by Prosecution in relation to the three accused. A large number of documents, approximately 4.000, was produced by the first ISU searches, and that was done by using the names of the three accused, as I understand it. The selection of these documents has already been disclosed to the Defence pursuant to Rules 66 and 68. And term searches are continuing and so disclosure of documents that will be produced by those searches. I also have been informed that at the last Status Conference in the Gotovina case, OTP said that after 18 April 2006 they would have put a large amount of material in the EDS system. I wonder if the Prosecution could be asked to report on the approximate number of statements now disclosed, the number of statements now translated, and the number of statements further envisaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As discussed at the 65 ter yesterday, Prosecution has disclosed to date approximately 520 statements. Those are -- those do not reflect 520 witnesses, because some witnesses provided more than one statement. There is approximately 415 witnesses. The statements, to the best of my knowledge, are translated. There are a number of documents, it's always hazardous to use a characterisation like "handful," but there are approximately 100 documents, I believe, that remain to be translated out of the approximately 2700 documents that were provided in connection with those witness statements. So I believe that the translation circumstances are effectively under control, and we obviously hope to be able to provide completed translations for those remaining documents at the earliest opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: And perhaps you could also comment on whether the disclosure of material in the Gotovina case has reached the same level as the disclosure in the Cermak and Markac case. Or if you want to add anything to the status of disclosure in relation to the accused Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. Again, the comments I make are subject to comments yesterday. So if I inadvertently omit some aspect of the disclosure situation that was clarified yesterday, it's not an effort to override that information yesterday. For the most part, the -- there's general parity in the disclosure situation. One of the distinctions that we noted yesterday was the fact that with respect to certain Rule 70 items, a specific request had to be initiated for the accused Gotovina, since the request for disclosure under Rule 70 must be specific to the individual. And so that is a relatively formalistic and perfunctory matter. We believe, and those will be -- I'm sure those authorisations will be forthcoming shortly. There are additional Rule 70 requests outstanding, again, as was discussed yesterday, but those apply to all three parties, and again those requests have been outstanding for some period of time. We will do our best to expedite those to the extent we're able to influence the governmental bureaucracies in the appropriate places and have those authorisations provided and the information disclosed as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. Does the Defence team for Gotovina have anything to add, any specific comments?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Luka Misetic on behalf of General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We agree with what the Prosecutor has said. We would add to points for the record, just to clarify. With respect to the search terms --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- the Prosecution is using in order to find documents the parties reached agreement yesterday whereby the Prosecution is going to provide all Defences with a copy of the search terms so the parties can, together, work to expedite the discovery and disclosure process. With respect to the issue of certain video and audio materials that have been disclosed to us, certain of those video and audio materials have not been transcribed and it was indicated to us by the Prosecution yesterday that those video and audio materials that are not provided in a transcribed form to us are an indication that the Prosecution does not intend to use those as part of its case. So with those two clarifications, I would say that the Prosecution has, indeed, accurately reflected what our agreement is from yesterday. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. And the Defence teams for Cermak?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have nothing to add to what Mr. Misetic has just said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further remarks, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. And Markac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Likewise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. As to the Rule 68, at the last Status Conference and during also yesterday's Rule 65 ter conference, the Prosecution stated that there has been disclosure of exculpatory material together with materials under Rule 66(A), that further searches are underway, and the Prosecution is aware that disclosure under Rule 68 is an ongoing obligation. From yesterday's discussion, it seems also that Defence of Markac will provide the Prosecution with suggestions of terms to be used in these searches. This is probably what we already have covered, is it? Yes. And Rule 70, this is also, I think, been commented on by the Prosecution side, and there was nothing further on this disclosure from the Defence side, Defence teams. As to agreed facts, I have been informed and I have full information on the submissions made by the parties. I have written -- I have read the different papers on this, and I understand, from the briefing that I have from yesterday's conference that Prosecution and Defence counsel for all three accused agree that it is preferable, it is better to wait for the final version of the indictment and, therefore, for the final resolution of the joinder issue by the Appeals Chamber. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that was -- that accurately reflects yesterday's discussion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, we agree with the Prosecution in that regard, Your Honour, on behalf of General Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Likewise, Your Honour. It's part of our agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Also, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. At the last Status Conference it was mentioned that one should really work -- make a work-plan, establish a work-plan for the further pre-trial preparations in this case. And it is my understanding from also yesterday's conference that this will take place and that at the next 65 ter conference the -- when we'll discuss with the parties and try definitely to elaborate a work-plan to secure that the trial can be starting as soon as possible, and this will be discussed then with the parties at this conference. Of course, this has also been affected, this intention to present a work-plan on this Status Conference has also been affected by the appeal on the joinder, and we really are waiting also on this point for -- as I understand it, for the decision by the Appeals Chamber. That's the correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, on both counts, I think. Both in terms of the impact of the pending issue but also in terms of the parties' commitment to work toward the establishment of a work-plan so that -- well, for the purposes the Court indicated. So it's correct that it had an immediate impact in terms of today's proceeding, but we will try to -- we will stay in contact both with the Senior Legal Officer and with the parties, with the development of a work-plan in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. Any comments on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just so the Court knows, I think it's something that has been discussed but it just makes it very difficult when, without some settlement of the final indictment, to make final decisions with regard to facts and work-plan, et cetera. So that that's the consensus of everybody yesterday with the court officers that that would be the way to go. And I don't think it is going to be a protracted period of time, Judge, until we get a final indictment to work from, so I guess all the parties just ask the Court to bear with us and get that final document settled, so then we can come up with a final work-plan and we come up with something that we're going to work with going forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Anything to add to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, nothing, Your Honour. Mr. Cermak's Defence shares this position and believes this to be the most realistic approach to the problem at hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Likewise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: I suppose that there has always -- that there has already been exchange of views on this subject of agreed facts, and hopefully this decision by the Appeals Chamber is not far away. I hope it will be here in the near future. And then the parties will then undertake an obligation to speed up this process on agreed facts, as I understand it. And that's to the Chamber's and to my satisfaction, that it is okay. Yes. And finally I would like to raise an issue that concerns all cases and that has to do with the translation. It is important, as I understand it, that the CLSS should be able to continue to provide translation in a timely fashion and meet the translation needs of all parties equitably. The policy of CLSS is to translate only documents which are submitted as evidence in Court. However, one of the main problems is that parties tend to submit translation requests of documents labelled as intended to be tendered as evidence, which they eventually do not tender. And I've been informed that on 24 August 2006 the bureau endorses various recommendations with special regard to the trials of multi-accused cases. And I just want to, in light of that, in view of that, remind the parties and the counsels the importance for the parties to limit their translation requests to those documents they will ultimately tender into evidence, prioritise translation requests, and make relevant information available to CLSS and ODM on a confidential basis. This is on the understanding of the parties. There is nothing controversial in this? No. Thank you. Then, as always on the Status Conferences, there is a question of, in this case, Gotovina, if there is any issues he wishes to raise as to his state of health or his conditions of detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Nothing with regard to his state of health. With regard to his conditions of detention, we have nothing to raise at this time. We do leave that as an open issue, Your Honour, to be addressed in the near future but not at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. I will make a note on that. And as for the accused Cermak and Markac, not present here today, do the Defence counsel have anything in particular they want to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Cermak seems to be experiencing some chronic problems with his spine and high blood pressure. It's all under control and being monitored by doctors. There are no major problems for the time being or for the future, in terms of being able to follow the trial, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. And for Markac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Markac is also experiencing some chronic problems. He received medical treatment while in detention. He is continuing this treatment and his health is now stable, with small fluctuations. He is under intensive care by a team of doctors, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, if there is no other issues that the parties want to raise, this Status Conference is over. For the Prosecution side? Nothing?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just -- I agree with the Court that the policy of the CLSS is that not a particularly controversial one and a very understandable one in light of their resource limitations. It is not entirely clear to me how that might play out for either party. In other words, whether documents submitted in good faith will be rejected without some particular kind of assurance. And furthermore what happens to documents that need to be -- the nature of which is such that they need to be translated before any realistic assessment can be made about whether or not they are to be admitted in court. It's something I raised yesterday. It seems to me that it's unlikely to result in pragmatic problems, but I just raise it now so that, to alert the Court that if it does, for either the Prosecution or for any of the Defence, then we may be coming back and bringing it to the Court's attention and trying to suggest some measures that will allow us to move forward expeditiously, notwithstanding the resource limitations of CLSS. That's all I wanted to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. Do the Defence teams have anything further, in light of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We understand what the problem is with CLSS. It's been a problem since day one in the Tribunal. We understand we're going to do the best we possibly can. Certainly we don't want to have anybody to do any work unnecessarily, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: You're in agreement?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing to add. Nothing to add, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STOLE
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. Then the Court now is adjourned, and I thank you for -- the accused Gotovina and the parties and the counsels for appearances here today. Thank you.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
